label: collenchymatous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a cell or a structure made of cells by virtue of the cell walls being thickened at the corners where the cells meet, as in collenchyma. NOTE: The bryological sense (leaf and exothecial cells); not the presence of PO:0005423 collenchyma tissue.
reason: In the moss floras this word describes cell-wall thickening, not tissue that is present, so a presence rule on collenchyma would be wrong. PATO has no term for cell walls thickened at the corners.
Exindusiate means the sori have no indusium. Built the same way as ebracteate = bract absent.

Calyculate means bearing a calyculus (an outer whorl of small bracts), and calyculus is a PO synonym of epicalyx. The rows on a petiole or leaf, and 'calicoïde' (calyx-like), are mis-assigned and should not use this rule.

label: hemi-epiphytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing as an epiphyte for part of its life and rooted in the ground for the other part, either starting on a host and sending roots down to the soil or starting in the soil and later losing its connection with it. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic; not a child of it, as the plant is not always epiphytic.
reason: This is a distinct, well-established habit (stranglers, aroid vines). Neither FLOPO epiphytic nor terrestrial covers it.

Spurless means the part has no spur. Lip and petal spurs are petal spurs, and on a flower the corolla spur (PO_0025512) should be used. PO has no general spur class, so the anther and sepal rows are not covered.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: square PATO_0000413 with rounded corners)
reason: This is two shape values joined into one word, like linear-lanceolate. It should be handled the way such compounds already are, not with a new term.

label: mitrate
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a mitre: a hollow, symmetric cone that is not split down one side, though it may be shortly lobed or split at the base on several sides. NOTE: Sibling and contrast of FLOPO:0991119 cucullate (calyptra split on one side).
reason: Mitrate versus cucullate is the standard character of the moss calyptra, and PATO has no mitre shape.
Aculeolate means bearing minute prickles, the small form of aculeate. The last review mapped aculeate to PATO spiny.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: rectangular PATO_0001867 + elongated PATO_0001154)
reason: This is two existing values run together to describe a cell outline. No new term is needed.
Efarinose is the negation of farinose, which the last review mapped to PATO mealy.
The examples mix unrelated senses: veins looping, spine bases joined by a membrane, fringe elements stuck together, and 'seemingly' webbed. No single quality fits them.
This is the negation of 'pitted', which the last review mapped to PATO foveate. For moss cell walls 'pitted' means wall pits rather than surface pits, so the rule is less certain there.
A sheathlike leaf or petiole base is one that forms a sheath round the stem, which is FLOPO sheathing. 'Lowermost leaves sheathlike' (leaves reduced to sheaths) fits less well.
Inflorescences 'capitulate' or 'en capitules' have their flowers in heads (FLOPO capitate). A capitulate stigma is head-shaped, which is a separate FLOPO term.
'False' qualifies a part name (false indusium, false vein, false stipule); it says the structure only resembles that part. It is not a quality of the bearer.
Ecostate means a moss leaf has no costa (PO costa is the non-vascular leaf midrib).
Homomallous moss leaves all turn towards one side, which is the definition of FLOPO secund.
For axes and veins, tenuous means slender; for leaves it means thin.
Cracking bark is FLOPO fissured, whose definition says 'marked by deep cracks' and which has cracked as a related synonym.
Carnose means fleshy. The 'sub-' prefix is handled by the approximate-value pattern (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md), as 'suborbicular' is.

target: new: value of a part of the bearer (claw of clawed FLOPO:0991169 + decreased length PATO_0000574)
reason: This combines clawed with a short length of the claw itself. That needs the quality placed on a part of the bearer, not a new term.
Basal veins coalesced for 1–2 cm are like parts fused together, which is FLOPO connate. The fused length is a measurement that goes with it.
Ebracteolate means without bracteoles, built the same way as ebracteate = bract absent.

label: pseudopetiolate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a leaf or leaflet by virtue of its blade narrowing at the base into a stalk-like part that is not a true petiole. NOTE: Contrast with FLOPO:0991023 petiolate; compare FLOPO:0991169 clawed.
reason: This is common in grasses, bamboos and monocots, and PO has no pseudopetiole part to state presence with. It could instead be modelled as the lamina base tapered (PATO_0001500), so a reviewer should check this.
Indument names a part, the covering of hairs. It is already a reviewed word for FLOPO indumentum (config/reviewed_local_bearers.tsv).
Acerose means needle-shaped. The last review mapped acicular the same way: PATO subulate, which has 'needle-like' as an exact synonym.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1: surface of the bearer; 'abaxial' is in config/flora_context_words.tsv)
reason: 'Abaxial' says where on the part a quality sits (the lower surface). That is already handled by the surface pattern, not by a quality term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: triangular PATO_0001875 + ovate) with degree 'narrowly'
reason: This is two existing shapes run together plus a word of degree ('narrowly'), so no term is needed.
Pinnately parted is the English form of pinnatipartite.

label: equitant
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being folded lengthwise and set astride the base of the next structure of its kind, so that the structures overlap in two opposite ranks. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991063 imbricate; the leaves are conduplicate (FLOPO:0991123).
reason: This is a distinct leaf arrangement (as in Iris), and PATO has no term for it. Neither imbricate nor conduplicate alone says it.
